method.git: not a git repository; branch N/A
method.inputs: existing bound TD reports, logs, SDC/ADC, current source hashes and local vendor public files
method.parser_checks: 20 displayed minimum paths parsed; arrival-required equals slack within 0.0011 ns; each has two clock records and two edge records

conclusions: Both historical standalone runs fail hold/removal: HWNS -1.742 ns, HTNS -175.425 ns. Setup +1.419 ns does not compensate.

Each run displays six asynchronous-reset removal paths, one clock-enable hold path, and three physical ima/imb data-input hold paths. All ten displayed startpoints are top-level input ports in this fixture.

Only 10 of 463 violating endpoints have displayed detail. The remaining 453 endpoint path classes, clock relationships and causes are unknown. 5734 analyzed paths is not a count of failing paths; 100% STA coverage is not 100% displayed-path coverage.

Baseline route already invokes native fix_hold once. The hold run adds a second explicit call. native_hold_repair=false in the summary means no extra script-level call, not absence of native hold optimization.

Both logs explicitly skip 409 abnormal routing timing paths under a disjunctive threshold rule. Their endpoint membership and individual trigger condition are unavailable; 409 paths cannot be equated to 409 of the 463 endpoints.

The two SDC files are byte-identical and contain no explicit false-path, multicycle, min/max-delay or clock-group exceptions. No bound report_timing_exception inventory is available, so effective exception completeness remains unknown.
Current source bytes match recorded historical source SHA at audit time. The project still references a mutable source path; this is not evidence of a preserved immutable source snapshot.

The final build report probe_route.timing is the primary detailed evidence. The internally generated final_timing.rpt minimum-path section is identical in each run. No improvement is observed in displayed paths or aggregate metrics after the extra fix_hold.

The observed clock insertion/arrival imbalance explains each listed numerical slack, but actual external phase, board pin placement and intended integrated launch boundary are not proven by this zero-delay standalone fixture.

Whether undisplayed same-clock register paths, CDC paths or other endpoint pin classes also violate
Whether alternate physical hold settings would improve timing without setup regression; not executed
A verified immutable historical RTL snapshot distinct from the mutable current source
next_steps_not_executed: Preserve these runs as failed evidence. Obtain exhaustive abnormal-target and violating-endpoint reports from their matching implementation database if available; verify artifact identity before any tool reuse.

Use the local TD report_abnormal_timing_target diagnostic named in PHY-5089 and report_timing_exception command documented in DefaultFlow.tcl, after verifying exact installed-version syntax and the matching routed database. Do not invent command arguments or silently launch TD.

Audit real synchronous upstream/downstream registers, clock topology and reset-release path. A registered-boundary probe is a separate implementation experiment, not proof that all old violations were I/O artifacts.

Only after path attribution, evaluate supported physical hold options with unchanged, justified timing requirements, and rerun setup/hold/recovery/removal/coverage together. Do not waive reset paths or tune external delays solely for a green report.
